entries.title: Light2D has no occlusion, so unexplored mine stays visible
entries.missing: A Light2D shines through solid Tilemap tiles: a miner's lamp lights the dirt behind the tunnel wall and, with the 16-lights cap, there is no fog of war or line of sight. A game whose point is exploring in the dark (Burrow Brigade) cannot keep the unseen parts black.
entries.workaround: A small lamp radius (96 world units, 20 when nearly dry), falloff 1.5 and SceneSettings.ambientLight 0.07, so the walls beyond a few tiles fall to near black. Walls next to the lamp still light up on the far side; a hand-made fog layer was not attempted in P1. P2: the fog of war grew on it: scripts/game/fog.js tracks seen tiles per miner and paints them on a second Tilemap.
entries.suggestion: Let a Light2D (or a Tilemap) opt into shadows from the solid tiles (a 2D shadow cast from Tilemap.solidTiles), or give Tilemap a per-tile 'explored' mask / fog-of-war layer that scripts can set.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.14 (Light2D on a light buffer: shadows from solid tiles and no 16-light cap) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 0d306a3c (M29.14): Light2D.castShadows and Tilemap.occludesLight make solid tiles cast shadows (rays traced per light, at most 32 lights cast shadows, new stat lights2dShadowed). Burrow Brigade keeps its own fog of war (fog.js): the fog is game state (seen, half dark, enemies drawn only on clear tiles), not only a look, and the game has not been switched to shadow casting, so it keeps the lamp radius, falloff and ambient light too.

entries.title: Tilemap tileset has no margin or spacing
entries.missing: Tilemap.tileset is cut into tileSize cells with no margin or spacing field. Kenney's Roguelike Caves & Dungeons sheet has a 1 px gap between tiles, so using it directly shows bleeding edges and shifted tiles.
entries.workaround: assets/src/make_atlases.py cuts the tiles out of the source sheets and re-packs them margin-free into assets/tiles_topsoil.png, tiles_crystal.png and tiles_magma.png and assets/sprites.png (run once, output committed).
entries.suggestion: Add Tilemap.margin and Tilemap.spacing (vec2, texture pixels), and the same for Sprite sheets in assets.generate_sprite_sheet / the editor tile picker.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.10 (Tilemap: tileset margin and spacing, setTile without rewriting the array) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 390af568 (M29.10): Tilemap.margin and Tilemap.spacing (pixels) are read by the 2D renderer, the tile count and validate. Burrow Brigade keeps its margin-free atlases (make_atlases.py, output committed): they work and re-cutting the art would change every tile and store screenshot for no gain in play.

entries.title: Changing one tile rewrites the whole Tilemap tiles array
entries.missing: Tilemap.tiles is one JSON value: digging a single tile means building and setting the full width*height array (up to 96x64 = 6144 integers here) through entity.set, and the renderer rebuilds the tilemap. There is no setTile.
entries.workaround: The shift keeps its own array, marks it dirty on every MineMap change and writes it once per frame in onLateUpdate, so several tiles dug in one frame cost one write. P2: the fog Tilemap and the flood and magma spreading rewrite tiles too, so scripts/game/fog.js and hazards.js batch their changes and write once per frame.
entries.suggestion: Expose a tile API on the Tilemap view: tilemap.setTile(tx, ty, index) / getTile, with a dirty-rect rebuild.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.10 (Tilemap: tileset margin and spacing, setTile without rewriting the array) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 390af568 (M29.10): tilemap.setTile(x, y, id) and getTile(x, y) change one tile in place (and 2D physics rebuilds only the changed colliders). Burrow Brigade dropped the dirty flag and the once-per-frame array write: shift.js sets each changed tile when the map changes (hazards go through the same map change), and fog.js sets one tile per changed fog state.

entries.title: Menu kit always adds the shop and the age gate
entries.missing: project.add_menu_kit creates a Shop button and panel, an age-gate script and prefab, shop strings and a purchases/ads check in main_menu.js even for a game with no store and no ads, and has no option to leave them out. validate does not complain about them but a first-time reader has to work out what to delete.
entries.workaround: Deleted the shop and age-gate files by hand, removed their imports, the shop_button handler and the 'ageGate' and 'shop' locale blocks from scripts/main_menu.js, scenes/menu.scene.json and locales/en.json.
entries.suggestion: Give project.add_menu_kit flags such as {"shop": false, "ageGate": false}, default true only when factoria.json declares purchases or ads.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.8 (Menu kit: optional shop and age gate, a Controls tab from the actions) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 2af58d1d (M29.8): the main menu no longer requires the shop and the age gate, and project.add_menu_kit adds them only when asked. Burrow Brigade's hand deletion was already done and stays (it has neither part); nothing was left to drop.

entries.title: Options Controls tab lists a hard-coded jump action
entries.missing: The kit's options.js rebinding list is a fixed array ['move_left','move_right','jump','pause'] with matching options.action.* strings, so a game with other actions (dig, move_up, move_down) shows a dead 'Jump' row and no rows for its own actions until the script and locale are edited.
entries.workaround: Edited the 'actions' list in scripts/ui/options.js and added options.action.move_up, move_down and dig to locales/en.json.
entries.suggestion: Build the list from input.actions() minus the ui_* ones, taking the label from options.action.<name> and falling back to the action name.
notes: 2026-10-25: Replaced the tab with a per-player page (a button cycles Player 1 to 4, six rows from controls.ACTIONS).
2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.8 (Menu kit: optional shop and age gate, a Controls tab from the actions) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 2af58d1d (M29.8): the Options Controls tab lists input.actions() without the ui_* ones, labelled with i18n.t, and Options.actions picks and orders them. Burrow Brigade keeps its own per-player Controls page in scripts/ui/options.js (one page per player, see FB-0006); the Options screen is being reworked by M29.19, so it was not touched here.

entries.title: Per-gamepad input cannot use actions, so co-op pads are not rebindable
entries.missing: Actions bound to Gamepad* names react to ANY connected pad. For local co-op each player needs their own pad, which only input.gamepad(i).axis/down answer, with raw button and axis names; those cannot go through the Options Controls rebinding or the per-action bindings in factoria.json.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/miner_input.js has three device kinds: 'any' (the project's actions: keyboard and every pad, one player), 'keys' (a fixed key block) and 'pad' (input.gamepad(i) with hard-coded left stick, d-pad and A/X). P2 added the torch button (B or Y on a pad, T on the keyboard) to the same three device kinds.
entries.suggestion: Per-player action sets: input.gamepad(i).down('dig') resolving the project's binding for that action, or input.player(i).axis(...) with a rebind per player.
notes: 2026-10-25: scripts/game/controls.js keeps a binding table per seat in settings.playerBindings (keys and pad families), miner_input.js reads it with input.keyDown and input.gamepad(i).down/axis by binding name; the Options Controls page is per player and captures input.lastPressed().
2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.15 (Per-player actions) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 4f6d6b63 (M29.15): input.player(i) gives each player their own actions bound to a pad or a key scheme, with pressed/held/axis, export/import of the rebinds and reset. Burrow Brigade's diggers read input.player(seat) (099f3d15: controls.js, miner_input.js, players.js) and its own binding table is gone.

entries.title: assets.synth_sound presets come out much louder than the validator accepts
entries.missing: Sounds from assets.synth_sound (ore, oil, lamp_out, rescue) measure between -3.8 and -7 LUFS, so 'factoria validate' warns 'very loud' and that they differ by 16 LU from the quieter presets.
entries.workaround: Set defaults.audio {normalize: true, targetLufs: -18} in assets.json so every effect plays at the same loudness.
entries.suggestion: Have synth_sound normalise its output to about -18 LUFS, or write the normalize import setting to assets.json itself.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.7 (Music: the scene-load bug, voice volume, synced layers, synth loudness) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 291f4b98 (M29.7): assets.synth_sound normalizes its presets to -18 LUFS, the loudness the validator accepts. Burrow Brigade keeps defaults.audio {normalize, targetLufs -18} in assets.json: it applies to every clip of the game, not only to synth presets.

entries.title: Light2D is capped at 16 per frame
entries.missing: Only 16 Light2D reach the shader per frame; more are dropped with no message and no way to choose which. A mine with torches, crystals and four miners' lamps goes past 16 at once.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/lights.js keeps a pool of 16 minus one per miner and gives it to the sources nearest the miners, switching the others off; tests count the active Light2D entities.
entries.suggestion: Pick the 16 lights that matter on the engine side (nearest the camera, brightest) and say so in the Light2D docs; or raise the cap with a tiled/clustered 2D lighting pass.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work packages M29.1 (Light2D in the stats and the perf budget, a better choice of 16) and M29.14 (Light2D on a light buffer) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in bef8abf1 (M29.1): the 16 kept lights are the ones that light the view (a light outside it is never kept over one inside), and more than 16 in view logs one warning per scene. On its own this did not let Burrow Brigade drop its pool.

Fixed in 0d306a3c (M29.14): lights render into a light buffer, so a frame keeps up to 256 Light2D. Burrow Brigade dropped the pool: lights.js gives every torch, crystal and magma source its own Light2D (no ENGINE_LIGHT_CAP, no ranking by distance to the miners), and the perf baselines now count the real lights (entities 144, lights 20, maxLights 24).

entries.title: renderStats().lights does not count Light2D
entries.missing: factoria:test renderStats().lights counts only 3D lights, so a test cannot assert how many Light2D are drawn or that the cap of 16 holds.
entries.workaround: tests/helpers/world.js activeLights() counts the active entities that carry a Light2D component instead of the lights the renderer uses.
entries.suggestion: Add lights2d (counted) and lights2dDropped to renderStats().
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.1 (Light2D in the stats and the perf budget, a better choice of 16); FB-0028 is a duplicate and its occurrences were merged here in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in bef8abf1 (M29.1): renderStats() has lights2d (drawn) and lights2dDropped (off view or over the budget of the frame), and perf.measure's lights, so maxLights, counts 2D lights. Burrow Brigade dropped its activeLights() helper: tests/light.test.js and tests/render_budget.test.js read lights2d and lights2dDropped, and the render budget test checks lights2d + lights2dDropped against the number of sources.

entries.title: No 2D or tile pathfinding
entries.missing: The engine has no path search for tile maps: enemies that chase a miner through tunnels that change as the miners dig need A* on the Tilemap that reacts to edits.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/pathfinding.js: A* over the mine grid (with dig cost, danger tiles, a path follower and a nav.version counter that tells followers when digging changed the map); tested in tests/pathfinding.test.js.
entries.suggestion: A nav module: nav.findPath(tilemap, from, to, opts) with a passable callback and an invalidation counter fed by Tilemap edits.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.11 (Tile pathfinding and a behaviour-tree module) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 23c2aae8 (M29.11): nav.findTilePath(tilemap | {width, height, cost}, from, to, {costs, diagonals, maxNodes, closest}) is A* on tile cells. Burrow Brigade's pathfinding.js no longer has its own A*: it builds a cost grid from MineMap.kinds and calls the engine, and keeps its dig costs, danger kinds and the follow-the-digging version counter.

entries.title: No behaviour tree or other AI module
entries.missing: The engine has no AI building blocks: enemies need sequences, selectors, cooldowns and interruption, and every game has to write them.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/behavior_tree.js is a small generic tree (sequence, selector, condition, action with hooks, wait, cooldown, inverter, succeeder); scripts/game/enemy_brains.js builds the beetle, thief and Mole King trees on it.
entries.suggestion: Ship a behaviour-tree helper in the scripting module, or document the pattern in AI_GUIDE.md.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.11 (Tile pathfinding and a behaviour-tree module) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 23c2aae8 (M29.11): import { bt } from "factoria" gives Tree, sequence, selector, condition, action, wait, cooldown, inverter, succeeder. Burrow Brigade deleted behavior_tree.js: enemy_brains.js builds the beetle, thief and Mole King trees with bt.

entries.title: Audio docs do not say a scene load stops the music
entries.missing: docs/AUDIO.md and the audio API say nothing about audio.music after a scene load. Only a paragraph on scene editing in AI_GUIDE.md says loading a scene stops the audio, so a track started in one scene silently ends in the next.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/music.js starts the stratum's track at every shift (play() always calls audio.music) and reports whether the track changed.
entries.suggestion: Say in the audio.music doc string and in AUDIO.md what a scene load does to music, and offer a persistent music option.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.7 (Music: the scene-load bug, voice volume, synced layers, synth loudness) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 291f4b98 (M29.7): loading a scene starts its music again (also when the track is the same as before) and audio.music(path, {persist: true}) keeps a track across loads; SCRIPTING.md and AI_GUIDE say a scene load stops sounds and music unless persisted. Burrow Brigade keeps music.play() calling audio.music at every shift: the shift picks the track of its stratum itself, so it needs no change.

entries.title: No split screen: one camera, no viewports
entries.missing: Only one Camera renders per frame; a second Camera, a viewport rectangle or a render target do not exist (docs list split-screen as roadmap). A co-op game cannot split into 2 to 4 views when the players part.
entries.workaround: scripts/game/camera_views.js computes the split plan (clusters, viewports, zoom, hysteresis) and follow_camera.js zooms one shared camera out up to a limit; a leash (limitMove) stops miners going farther than the largest view. The plan is published and tested but not drawn.
entries.suggestion: Camera.viewport [x,y,w,h] normalised, several primary cameras per frame, each with its own Light2D culling and HUD space.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.19 (Split screen: camera viewports) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in f8ddc3e9 (M29.19): one render loop per active primary camera into its Camera.viewport (up to 8), and the screen conversions take a camera. Burrow Brigade: camera_views.js's plan is now drawn, one Camera per view made by follow_camera.js, when Options > Video > Split screen when players part is on (off by default); the leash (limitMove) stays only when it is off.

entries.title: No gamepad connect/disconnect events and no stable pad identity
entries.missing: input.gamepad(i).connected can only be polled, there is no event, and a pad that is unplugged and plugged in may come back in another slot with nothing to tell which pad it was.
entries.workaround: pad_watch.js polls connected every frame, pauses with a prompt, resumes on reconnect and lets a free pad (A) or the keyboard (Enter) take the miner over; join.js polls the four slots.
entries.suggestion: input.on('gamepadConnected'|'gamepadDisconnected', {index, id}) and a stable pad id string (vendor/product/serial) on input.gamepad(i).
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.9 (Gamepad connect events, a stable pad id and Steam Deck detection) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in fe840536 (M29.9) and M29.15 (padId): game.on("gamepadConnected" | "gamepadDisconnected") with the slot and a stable id, and a returning pad gets its old slot when it is free. Burrow Brigade now uses them: players.js keeps each pad player's padId (input.player(i).use({ padId }), so the miner reads its own pad whatever slot it is in) and pad_watch.js listens to gamepadConnected to move a player's device.index when its pad comes back in another slot, so the pause screen clears by itself (test: coop.test.js, 'a pad that comes back in another slot'). Still polled on purpose: pad_watch.js reads input.gamepad(i).connected every frame (pads plugged in when the scene starts are not announced, and a state read cannot be missed) and join.js reads the button presses of the four slots, which are state, not events.

entries.title: Steam Remote Play Together guests are not exposed
entries.missing: Steam shows a Remote Play guest's controller as one more gamepad, but the game cannot tell it from a local pad, nor ask Steam which seats are guests, nor use Steam Input glyphs per player.
entries.workaround: join.js and pad_watch.js treat every pad the same and poll, so a guest pad that appears mid-lobby joins with A; tested with a pad connected during the lobby on the test API (no fake Steam store hook exists for it).
entries.suggestion: platform.steam.remotePlay: {guests: [{index, name}]} plus an event, and the fake store able to add guests.
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.18 (Steam Remote Play guests and cloud.stat) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in cd8fb526 (M29.18): a remotePlay service (sessions(), connect and disconnect events, a fake for tests). Burrow Brigade does not read it: a guest's controller reaches the game as an ordinary pad, so join.js and pad_watch.js treat it like any other pad and keep their workaround.

entries.title: Scripts cannot read or write the system clipboard
entries.missing: No clipboard API in the factoria module and no paste shortcut in TextField, so a seed code cannot be copied to another program or pasted from one
entries.workaround: scripts/game/clipboard.js keeps a session buffer behind copy()/paste() and a useSystem({write,read}) hook; the camp and results say honestly when the code only stayed in the game; the title has a Paste button that reads the buffer; scripts/game/text_entry.js (P5) cleans a typed code to an alphabet without 0/O/1/I, so a code read aloud or from a screen is typed back without mistakes
entries.suggestion: clipboard.read()/clipboard.write(text) in the factoria module (async on web), and Ctrl+V / Cmd+V in a focused TextField
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.4 (The clipboard and the window-close event) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in d025e515 (M29.4): clipboard.read() (a Promise) and clipboard.write(text) with window.supports("clipboard"); a focused TextField pastes with Ctrl/Cmd+V and copies with Ctrl/Cmd+C. Burrow Brigade's clipboard.js writes and reads the system clipboard (the title's Paste button checks that its scene is still current after the read) and keeps a session buffer only where there is no script clipboard (phones); text_entry.js still cleans typed codes.

entries.title: game.today() has no time of day, so the UTC date is not derivable
entries.missing: game.today() answers the local calendar date and utcOffsetMinutes, but no hour or minute, so a daily seed that must roll over at the same instant for every player (UTC midnight) cannot be computed
entries.workaround: scripts/game/daily.js keys the daily dig on the local date (game.today().iso); players in other time zones roll over at their own midnight, and the README says so
entries.suggestion: add utcIso (the UTC date) or hour/minute to game.today(), still fixed by game.setDate in tests
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.2 (The time of day in game.today() and a daily leaderboard by date) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 120550c2 (M29.2): game.today() has hour, minute, second, utcOffsetMinutes and a utc date, and a dayChanged event. Burrow Brigade's daily dig is keyed on game.today().utc.iso, so everybody in the world plays the same mine on the same UTC day, and its README no longer says the key is local.

entries.title: platform.cloud has no modified time or conflict signal
entries.missing: cloud.load answers only the value: no modified time, device id or conflict notice, so two devices that played offline cannot be told apart by the store
entries.workaround: scripts/game/cloud.js stores a revision counter in every save and the revision last synced per slot (burrow.cloudBase.N), settles a conflict by play time and keeps the loser as burrow.backup.N
entries.suggestion: cloud.stat(key) answering { modified, size } and a conflict event where the store has one (Steam Cloud, iCloud)
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.18 (Steam Remote Play guests and cloud.stat) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in cd8fb526 (M29.18): platform.cloud.stat(key) returns the size and modified time of a cloud file (Steam GetFileTimestamp, Play snapshot metadata; null time on Apple). Burrow Brigade keeps its revision counter and burrow.cloudBase.N in cloud.js: it works on every store, including Apple where there is no modified time.

entries.title: game.click on a widget of a panel opened in the same frame silently does nothing
entries.missing: Right after a panel becomes active, ui.rectOf answers the default rectangle until one game.step has laid it out, and game.click(id) then hits nothing without any message
entries.workaround: tests step twice after opening a panel before clicking in it (tests/cloud.test.js, tests/saves.test.js)
entries.suggestion: game.click throws 'widget not laid out yet: step once after activating it'
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.6 (Test runner and ui.check_layout) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in edb178ec (M29.6): game.click lays the UI out first and throws, naming the widget, when it is not laid out or not visible. Burrow Brigade's saves and cloud tests dropped the extra steps after opening the slots panel; the steps that wait for an answer stay.

entries.title: No HTTP, news, remote-config or analytics API
entries.missing: A game script cannot fetch a JSON file or post an event: there is no http/fetch API, no news feed, no remote config and no analytics service in the engine
entries.workaround: scripts/game/online.js is a transport seam (offline by default, a fake in tests); news, balance and analytics go through it, and every feature works offline. A real transport has to be plugged in when the engine offers one
entries.suggestion: A promise-based http module with timeouts and a test fake (game.http), plus a consent-aware analytics.track
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work packages M29.20 (http.fetch on every platform) and M29.21 (Analytics with consent and remote config) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 94047d90 (M29.20): http.fetch(url, {method, headers, body, timeout}) on every platform, with a fake in tests and headless runs that answers what game.platform.respond gives it. Burrow Brigade does not call it directly; news and balance reach the network through the engine services below.

Fixed in 1c0beff9 (M29.21): analytics.event with the player's consent, batched and flushed on suspend and quit, and remoteConfig.get(key, default) fetched at start and cached. Burrow Brigade dropped its transport seam: online.js is now a thin wrapper over remoteConfig (news.js and balance.js read it), analytics.js records events on the engine's analytics service, and every feature still works offline.

entries.title: A daily leaderboard cannot be targeted by date
entries.missing: A leaderboard with period daily picks its day from game.today() at the moment of the post, and leaderboards.submit has no way to name a day, so a daily-seed try that began before midnight and ends after it posts to the next day's board, and a game that keys its daily seed by UTC (the usual choice for a worldwide daily) cannot post to the matching board
entries.workaround: scripts/game/boards.js posts to the daily board only when run.dailyKey (the local date the try began on, scripts/game/daily.js) is within one day of game.today().iso and records lastPost.daily.skipped otherwise
entries.suggestion: leaderboards.submit(id, score, {day:'YYYY-MM-DD'}) or game.today() with a utc option
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.2 (The time of day in game.today() and a daily leaderboard by date) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 120550c2 (M29.2): leaderboards.submit(id, score, {day}) and entries(id, {day}) address the daily board of a UTC day. Burrow Brigade posts a daily run to the board of run.dailyKey and reads the board of today's UTC day, so a try that crosses midnight posts to the day it began on; the otherDay skip is gone.

entries.title: No Steam Deck detection API
entries.missing: No platform.isSteamDeck or device query; only a connected pad of type steamdeck says the game runs on a Deck
entries.workaround: scripts/game/deck.js isDeck() looks for a connected pad of type steamdeck, so a Deck driven by the keyboard or touch is not detected
entries.suggestion: platform.device with {steamDeck, handheld}
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.9 (Gamepad connect events, a stable pad id and Steam Deck detection) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in fe840536 (M29.9): game.device.steamDeck and game.device.handheld (the Steam plugin, else the SteamDeck environment variable); game.setDevice takes them in tests. Burrow Brigade's isDeck() is game.device.steamDeck, so a Deck driven by the keyboard or touch is detected too.

entries.title: No quit or window-close event
entries.missing: game.on has suspend and resume but no quit event, so a game cannot send a last message when the window closes
entries.workaround: Only the Quit button of the title flushes the analytics (scripts/main_menu.js quit()); closing the window loses the unsent events, which stay queued only in memory
entries.suggestion: game.on('quit', fn) with a short grace period
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.4 (The clipboard and the window-close event) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in d025e515 (M29.4): game.on("quit") is raised by the close button, Cmd+Q and Alt+F4 (a handler may cancel); with M29.21 the analytics queue is sent on every way out of the game, within 3 seconds. Burrow Brigade no longer flushes by hand; the Quit button only queues its "quit" event (analytics.recordQuit), and closing the window loses nothing that waits.

entries.title: The test runner cannot press Enter on a TextField
entries.missing: game.press only takes input actions and TextField ignores ui_submit, so a test cannot submit a TextField
entries.workaround: tests/deck.test.js checks onChange only; onSubmit in text_entry.js is used the same way and is untested
entries.suggestion: game.pressKey('Enter') or game.submit(id)
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.6 (Test runner and ui.check_layout) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in edb178ec (M29.6): game.tapKey(key) presses and releases a key over one frame, so game.tapKey("Enter") submits a TextField. Burrow Brigade's tests/deck.test.js now tests text_entry's onSubmit with it.

entries.title: No layered or synced music, and a playing voice's volume cannot change
entries.missing: audio.music is one stream and the volume of a voice that plays cannot be changed, so a danger layer and a fight layer cannot fade in over the track of the stratum
entries.workaround: scripts/game/music.js plays one-bar loops of each layer on the bar lines of a real-time clock and starts or stops them as a chase rises or falls; the layers never fade, they come and go on the bar
entries.suggestion: audio.musicLayers({name: path}) with setLayer(name, volume, fadeSeconds), all layers sample-synced; or a volume that audio.setVoiceVolume(handle, v, fade) can change
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.7 (Music: the scene-load bug, voice volume, synced layers, synth loudness) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 291f4b98 (M29.7): audio.musicLayers({name: path}, opts) starts several tracks on the same sample, audio.setLayer(name, volume, fade) mixes them, and audio.setVoiceVolume changes a playing voice. Burrow Brigade keeps its emulation (music.js): its layers are one-bar loops (make_music_layers.py), not full-length stems, so using musicLayers means re-rendering and listening to the music; it was not done in this pass.

entries.title: No bus effects, ducking or snapshots
entries.missing: The audio API has bus volumes only: no low-pass filter, reverb, ducking or named mixer snapshots, so a paused game, water or a big cave cannot change the sound
entries.workaround: scripts/game/mix.js owns the four bus volumes (user volume x snapshot factor x duck) and eases them; muffling is just quieter and the cavern echo is a delayed, quieter replay of the clip in scripts/game/sound.js
entries.suggestion: audio.bus(name).lowpass / reverb / duck({by, depth, seconds}) and audio.snapshot(name, {fadeSeconds}) over a table the game defines
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.16 (Bus effects, ducking and snapshots) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 44c0bc69 (M29.16): audio.bus(name).lowpass(hz), .reverb(mix), .duck(byBus, amount, attack, release) and audio.snapshot(name, {fade}). Burrow Brigade keeps mix.js and the replayed echo in sound.js: moving to real filters and reverb changes how the game sounds and needs listening, so it was not done in this pass.

entries.title: The window API has no borderless mode and no monitor choice
entries.missing: window.setFullscreen takes a boolean (the window covering the monitor), so Options cannot offer windowed / borderless / exclusive fullscreen, or choose the monitor
entries.workaround: Options > Video offers windowed and full screen only, and shows the monitor's size as text (scripts/ui/options.js)
entries.suggestion: window.setMode('windowed' | 'borderless' | 'fullscreen') and window.monitors / window.setMonitor(i)
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.17 (Monitor choice and window modes) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 7156bfaf (M29.17): window.monitors(), window.setMonitor(i) and window.setMode("windowed" | "borderless" | "fullscreen") on Windows, macOS and Linux. Burrow Brigade now uses them: Options > Video cycles the three modes with window.setMode (borderless only where window.supports("borderless")) and shows a monitor button (window.monitors() / window.setMonitor) only where window.supports("monitors") and there is more than one monitor; settings.js saves displayMode and monitor and applies them at start, and an older save's fullscreen flag still means full screen.

entries.title: renderStats, perf.measure and maxLights do not count Light2D
entries.missing: renderStats().lights counts 3D lights only. In a 2D game with 16 Light2D lamps perf.measure reports lights 0 and the maxLights budget guards nothing
entries.workaround: tests/render_budget.test.js counts the active Light2D entities itself (cap 16) on the busiest floor, next to the draw call and entity budgets
entries.suggestion: Count Light2D in renderStats().lights (or add light2d) and let perf.json maxLights apply to both
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: duplicate of FB-0009 (its occurrences were merged there); work package M29.1 (Light2D in the stats and the perf budget, a better choice of 16) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in bef8abf1 (M29.1), as FB-0009: perf.measure's lights and so the maxLights budget count 2D lights. Burrow Brigade's render budget test reads renderStats().lights2d instead of counting entities, and perf.json holds the real count (lights 20, maxLights 24).

entries.title: The exported player has no input replay, state dump or screenshot option
entries.missing: factoria_player accepts only [projectDir|game.pak] --scene --fullscreen --frames --version, so an exported build cannot be driven by a replay or asked for its state; 'it starts and takes input' cannot be proven on the exported binary itself
entries.workaround: SHIPPING.md: the exported app is smoke-tested with --frames (exit 0, logs the scene load), input is proven by factoria run --headless --input with a state dump on the same project and scripts; the real keyboard and pad run on the exported build is a manual check
entries.suggestion: Give factoria_player --input FILE, --state-out FILE and --screenshot-at in a release build too (headless or windowed), or document that the player is not testable
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.13 (The exported player takes an input replay, dumps its state and takes a screenshot) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 78e12e7a (M29.13): the exported player accepts --input, --dump-state and --screenshot with --frames through the same options as factoria run. Burrow Brigade's SHIPPING.md says so; its check with factoria run stays as written because no export was made in this pass.

entries.title: No way to start a scene with parameters or to record an input replay
entries.missing: A scene cannot be given arguments from the command line or factoria call, and nothing records the keys and pads of a real or bot-driven session into a replay JSON
entries.workaround: A generated scene per shot (store/make_store.py) holds a script with literal props; store/record.test.js drives MinerBots under factoria test and prints @@REPLAY lines the script turns into replays; scripts/game/busiest.js reads an override export for tests
entries.suggestion: factoria run --prop name=value (read through an engine API) and input.record(path) that writes the replay format
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.12 (input.record and starting a scene with props) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 21ce220b (M29.12): input.record {action: start | stop} records keys, mouse, touches and gamepads into a replay, and scene.load(path, props) with game.sceneProps() hands values to a scene. Burrow Brigade keeps its generated store scenes and its bot-made replays (store/record.test.js): they work and were not regenerated in this pass.

entries.title: A declared Steam plugin without Valve's library logs an ERROR on every run and blocks the other platforms' exports
entries.missing: platform.add_backend steam writes plugins/steam, but the library libsteam_api for each OS comes from Valve's SDK, which is not redistributable. Without it every run logs an ERROR and validate warns that the windows and linux plugin builds are missing
entries.workaround: plugins/steam is not committed (.gitignore); SHIPPING.md says to run platform.add_backend with sdk on each build machine before exporting. Without it the game runs with platform services off
entries.suggestion: Let a plugin be optional per platform (skip with an INFO when the library is missing) or keep the backend declaration apart from the build of the library
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.5 (Steam from one Mac: optional plugin, exports, app 480, capsules) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in f96d04d3 (M29.5): a plugin that cannot load its library logs a warning instead of an ERROR, and project.export takes allowMissingPlugins. Burrow Brigade still does not commit plugins/steam and SHIPPING.md keeps the platform.add_backend step for the machine that exports.

entries.title: The installed windows, linux and mobile players carry no build fingerprint
entries.missing: Players in ~/.factoria/players/0.2.0 for windows, linux and mobile have no build fingerprint, so export refuses them as a mismatch with this factoria
entries.workaround: export with --allow-player-mismatch for windows and linux and say in SHIPPING.md that those two builds were not run
entries.suggestion: Stamp the fingerprint when a player is built or fetched, or compare by engine version when it is absent
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.5 (Steam from one Mac: optional plugin, exports, app 480, capsules) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in f96d04d3 (M29.5): a player with no build fingerprint gets its own error that does not point at setup players. Burrow Brigade keeps exporting windows and linux with --allow-player-mismatch, because only the 0.2.0 player is installed here.

entries.title: publish.steam refuses app 480 even in a dry run
entries.missing: A project that uses Valve's test app 480 (the only id available before paying the Steam fee) cannot see the upload plan: the dry run fails with 'a build cannot be uploaded to it'
entries.workaround: The dry run is shown with an explicit appId placeholder (factoria call publish.steam '{"dryRun":true,"appId":1234567}'); steam_appid.txt keeps 480 for the Spacewar check
entries.suggestion: Allow dryRun with app 480 (print the plan and a warning) and refuse only the real upload
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.5 (Steam from one Mac: optional plugin, exports, app 480, capsules) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in f96d04d3 (M29.5): publish.steam accepts app 480 in a dry run with a warning and still refuses it for a real upload. Burrow Brigade's SHIPPING.md says so; the dry run it shows still uses another id because it was not rerun.

entries.title: No way to frame a still of the game from a camera that follows the players
entries.missing: The key art needs the four miners, their lights and the camp in one composed frame, but the camera follows the miners and the capsule logo covers the middle; assets.draw_capsules only crops the key art by a focus point
entries.workaround: store/make_store.py renders a staged keyart scene, lifts the picture with PIL (KEYART_LIFT) so the logo sits below the miners, then calls assets.draw_capsules
entries.suggestion: assets.draw_capsules option for a safe area or a logo anchor so the focus keeps the subject clear of the logo
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.5 (Steam from one Mac: optional plugin, exports, app 480, capsules) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in f96d04d3 (M29.5): assets.draw_capsules takes logoAnchor and safeArea per capsule, and focus also moves the logo. Burrow Brigade keeps the picture lift (KEYART_LIFT) in make_store.py: the capsules were not redrawn in this pass.

entries.title: A test cannot write a file, so a recording has to go through stdout
entries.missing: factoria test scripts have no file-writing API, so a bot session cannot save the replay it produced
entries.workaround: store/record.test.js prints one @@REPLAY JSON line per floor and make_store.py parses them out of the test output
entries.suggestion: A files.write under the project's build/ folder available to tests (tools already have project files)
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.6 (Test runner and ui.check_layout) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in edb178ec (M29.6): SCRIPTING.md shows fa.call("fs.write", {path, content}) to save a file from a test. Burrow Brigade's store/record.test.js writes each recording to .factoria/tmp with it and make_store.py reads those files; the @@REPLAY lines in stdout are gone.

entries.title: Text wrapping cannot break Thai (or Khmer, Lao, Burmese) at word boundaries
entries.missing: The text engine wraps only at an ASCII space, U+3000 and between CJK characters. A Thai sentence is written without spaces, so it is one unbreakable run: it overflows its maxWidth or is cut. ZWSP, thin and hair spaces are not break opportunities either
entries.workaround: The Thai table writes a real space between phrases and keeps every space-free run under 17 base letters, checked by a test and by tools/thai_spaces.py
entries.suggestion: Break opportunities at ZWSP (U+200B) and WORD JOINER-free runs, or a dictionary-free Thai/Khmer/Lao/Burmese break iterator (ICU-style); then a locale could carry ZWSP between words
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.3 (Thai line breaks at marked boundaries and the sara am check) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 2690d768 (M29.3): text wrapping breaks after U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE (not drawn) and the UAX 14 spaces, so Thai text whose translator marks word boundaries wraps there; breaking unmarked Thai needs a dictionary and is not done. Burrow Brigade keeps its real spaces between phrases and the 17-letter check (thai_spaces.py): it has no word-marked Thai text.

entries.title: localization validate's glyph check misses U+0E4D that Thai sara am (U+0E33) needs
entries.missing: Thai sara am is drawn as U+0E4D + U+0E32 by the text engine, but validate's glyph check only looks for U+0E33, so a font subset without U+0E4D passes validate and shows a missing-glyph box at run time
entries.workaround: The font subset script keeps U+0E4D explicitly and checks the decomposed forms (assets/fonts/make_subset.py --check)
entries.suggestion: Run the glyph check on the characters the shaper actually draws (after the decomposition), or document it in docs/LOCALIZATION.md
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.3 (Thai line breaks at marked boundaries and the sara am check) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in 2690d768 (M29.3): the glyph check expands composed vowels (U+0E33 needs U+0E4D and U+0E32), and localization validate and the missing-glyph warning name them. Burrow Brigade keeps keeping U+0E4D in make_subset.py: it is the step that builds the font, and the engine check now agrees with it.

entries.title: ui.check_layout ignores ScrollList clipping and sees only scenes as they settle
entries.missing: check_layout reports an overlap for a widget inside a ScrollList that is clipped away (the Russian camp at 200 % reports a shop row under the buttons below the list), and it cannot see the panels a script opens later (slots, Options, boards, credits, pause)
entries.workaround: tests/helpers/layout.js reads ui.state (rectangles, overflowed) and clips by ScrollList ancestors; tests/layout.test.js drives every script-opened panel; the one known false positive is filtered by name
entries.suggestion: Clip a widget's rectangle by its ScrollList ancestors in check_layout, and accept a list of steps (clicks) per scene to reach a state before checking
notes: 2026-10-25 triage: confirmed open; work package M29.6 (Test runner and ui.check_layout) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

Fixed in edb178ec (M29.6): ui.check_layout intersects each widget with its ScrollList's clip and takes steps per scene (clicks, keys, frames) before the checks. Burrow Brigade keeps tests/helpers/layout.js: it also checks overlaps and panel containment at three languages and two text sizes, which its layout tests rely on.
